_comment: Connector-specific edits to GENERATED files that a cli-printing-press reprint must NOT clobber. check_handfixes.py asserts every marker below is still present (and banned anti-patterns absent) and fails CI if a reprint dropped one. Provenance: project_nerdio_print_gotchas.md (first print 2026-06-06, press 4.22.0, NMM Partner API). NOTE the NERDIO_*-MCP binary still ships the -pp- name (peer fleet drift, passes verify_all) - that is NOT a hand-fix and is deliberately not asserted here.

handfixes.summary: All 5 env vars (NERDIO_BASE_URL, NERDIO_TOKEN_URL, NERDIO_OAUTH_SCOPE + CLIENT_ID/SECRET) are in manifest.json user_config/mcp env + server.json + docs; the press documented only the 2 auth.env_vars
handfixes.why: Per-instance oauth2 trap variant: config.go reads FIVE vars but the press generator documents only CLIENT_ID/SECRET (auth.env_vars) in README env table, mcpb user_config, server.json, and doctor checks. Without BASE_URL/TOKEN_URL/OAUTH_SCOPE the .mcpb extension and every documented env example point at nothing and fail. Hand-added to manifest user_config + mcp_config.env + server.json + docs. A reprint drops the three non-auth vars again. Cousin of hudu/n-central per-instance BASE_URL omission.
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: Fix belongs in the press: per-instance oauth2 connectors should derive the full required-var set (base_url/token_url/scope) for docs + manifest, not just auth.env_vars. Doctor still only checks 2 (retro candidate).

handfixes.summary: Docs warn NERDIO_OAUTH_SCOPE is the bare '<app-id>/.default' with NO api:// prefix (api:// triggers AADSTS500011)
handfixes.why: Nerdio's correct AAD scope is the bare Application ID URI default with no api:// prefix; adding api:// triggers AADSTS500011 (Nerdio's own docs got this wrong for years). The press has no knowledge of this Azure-AD quirk, so the hand-authored guide.md/SKILL.md note is the only place a user learns it. A reprint regenerates the docs without the warning.

handfixes.summary: Reserved framework command `jobs` renamed to `job` (singular, matches /job/{id}); novel scripted-actions dup-parent (TODO stub) removed
handfixes.why: (1) `jobs` is a reserved framework command, so the spec resource was renamed to `job` (singular, matches the API path /job/{id}). (2) The novel emitter resolved the existing parent by derived filename (scripted_actions.go underscore) and missed the generated scripted-actions.go (hyphen), creating TWO Cobra parents with Use 'scripted-actions', the novel one showing 'TODO: implement' in root help. The duplicate novel parent file + its root.go registration were deleted; the generated Hidden parent already AddCommands the novel subcommand. A reprint reintroduces both the reserved-name collision and the duplicate TODO parent.
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: (1) `job` rename is spec-encoded (x-pp-resource); keep it on re-copy. (2) The dup-parent is a press novel-emitter bug (filename hyphen/underscore mismatch) - filed/file as a retro so the emitter resolves parents structurally, not by derived filename.

handfixes.summary: doctor probes a real GET endpoint with the real credential and refuses to dial a placeholder base_url, instead of calling any HTTP response 'reachable' and never checking the credential
handfixes.why: `doctor` is the command every SKILL, guide and docs page tells an operator to run to confirm the connector works, and it could not tell a working install from a broken one. It called any HTTP response to `GET /` "reachable" and rendered it green, so a base_url aimed at the vendor's web UI (where every API path 404s) and a token rejected with 401 on every call both produced an all-green report. On this connector family it also never probed the credential at all: it printed "present, not verified" and left the operator to guess. The mirror defect: a connector whose shipped base_url default is a placeholder dialled the placeholder host, and the DNS failure rendered as "FAIL API: unreachable" - telling a correctly-credentialled operator they were broken without naming the one variable that would fix it. Several placeholder hosts resolve through live wildcard DNS and answer real HTTP, so dialling one produced a confident green verdict against a stranger's server. Measured and gated by tools/maintainer/check_doctor_truth.py. See issue #282.

asserts.contains: report["credentials"] = "ERROR not verified: no credential is configured, so nothing was probed."
report["api"] = "not configured (base_url is a placeholder); set " + doctorBaseURLEnv + " to your own instance URL"

handfixes.summary: every operator credential this connector reads is declared on all three install channels: manifest.json (.mcpb), server.json (MCP Registry) and mcp-install.md (manual install)
handfixes.why: Issue #282 ('three live-verified connectors prompt for the wrong credentials'). A connector is installed through THREE independent channels that each carry their own copy of the credential list: manifest.json server.mcp_config.env (what the .mcpb bundle hands Claude Desktop, which has no shell profile, no config.toml and no export - so an undeclared variable is a variable nobody is ever asked for), server.json environmentVariables (the MCP Registry publish channel), and mcp-install.md's copy-paste JSON blocks plus its remote launch line (the manual path, which never touches the bundle at all). The fleet-wide audit found 60 of 65 connectors under-declaring 122 operator-facing variables in the manifest, 61 of 65 mcp-install.md pages omitting 125, and hudu's server.json missing the base URL its manifest marks required. mcp-install.md's env blocks gained: NERDIO_BASE_URL, NERDIO_TOKEN_URL. manifest.json, server.json and mcp-install.md are ALL regenerated by /msp-skills-publish on an UPDATE or re-onboard, so without this ledger a regeneration silently drops every declaration and CI stays green (check_env_schema.py is wired --warn). The asserts below name the specific credentials, not a count, so dropping one and adding another cannot cancel out.
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: cli-printing-press should emit server.mcp_config.env, the matching user_config prompts, server.json environmentVariables and mcp-install.md's env blocks from ONE declaration of the connector's operator-facing environment, so the three channels cannot be generated out of step. Until then check_env_schema.py compares all three and this ledger pins them.

handfixes.summary: NERDIO_NO_CONFIG_WRITE makes every credential write a no-op (token cache included) while leaving the `auth logout` erase working, and the MCP server honours it too (issue #270)
handfixes.why: Issue #270, raised by @Xenith-B off the back of #266. #266 stopped env-supplied client credentials reaching disk; the MINTED access token still landed in ~/.config/<tool>-cli/config.toml in cleartext and there was no supported way to turn that off. Their workaround was `--config NUL`, which is OS-specific, undocumented, makes doctor report a false 'not configured', and - the part that matters most - does not cover the MCP servers at all, because internal/mcp resolved its own hardcoded config path and ignored --config. Three deliberate boundaries make this switch honest rather than merely quiet. (1) ClearTokens keeps calling save() directly: it is the ERASE path, and routing it through the guard would make `auth logout` silently inert, which is a worse defect than the one being fixed. (2) `auth login` and `auth set-token` REFUSE and name the variable rather than reporting a save that did not happen - a false success is the same defect class as a doctor that says credentials are fine without checking. (3) newMCPClient now resolves through config.Load(""), the resolver the CLI uses, so the MCP server honours both NERDIO_CONFIG and this switch; that is the half the issue says is uncovered today. The variable is declared on all three install channels because for a Claude Desktop install the manifest prompt is the ONLY channel that can set an environment variable. Class C, new documented surface. GENERATOR-class: a reprint drops the switch entirely and silently restores the plaintext token cache. The tests run in the press sandbox (testenv.Isolate): setting only HOME let Windows resolve the credentials file under USERPROFILE, outside the test's snapshot (Windows CI on PR #577).
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: cli-printing-press should emit <PREFIX>_NO_CONFIG_WRITE (or an equivalent) as part of the standard config surface, with the same three boundaries: the erase path exempt, explicit save commands failing loudly rather than no-oping, and the MCP server resolving its config through config.Load("") instead of a hardcoded home-relative path. The hardcoded path in internal/mcp/tools.go is a generator defect in its own right - it makes --config and <PREFIX>_CONFIG inert for every MCP install on every connector.

asserts.contains: | `auth login` / `auth set-token` | Refuse, naming the variable, instead of reporting a save that did not happen. |

handfixes.summary: --dry-run never mints a token or changes stored credentials: neither the client's automatic client-credentials mint nor `auth login --dry-run` sends the client secret to the token URL, and `auth set-token --dry-run` and `auth logout --dry-run` neither save nor clear anything
handfixes.why: tools/maintainer/class_harness.py write-safety found every --dry-run of a write command putting one request on the wire: authHeader ran before the dry-run branch and, with no cached token, POSTed the client ID and secret to the token URL and cached the token, while the generated comment and the docs say a dry run sends nothing. `auth login` minted through its own path and ignored --dry-run, and `auth set-token` and `auth logout` saved and cleared credentials under --dry-run (found by Codex review round 1). Same fix shape as connectwise-rmm, sophos-central and watchguard (dry-run-never-mints). TestDryRunNeverMintsAToken, TestAuthLoginDryRunSendsNothing and TestAuthSetTokenAndLogoutHonorDryRun count requests to a stub token server (each with a live control that proves the probe reaches the mint) and fail on the generated code.
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: Press fix: client.go.tmpl should skip the client-credentials mint when DryRun is set (the dry-run preview already uses cached material only), and auth.go.tmpl's login should honor the root --dry-run flag.

handfixes.summary: Every token request (auth login, the automatic client-credentials mint and the refresh grant) goes through cliutil.OAuthTokenHTTPClient, which follows same-origin redirects only, so the client secret never reaches a host a redirect from the token URL names
handfixes.why: Owner decision on PR #441 (finish the auth-wire class). `auth login` (through http.DefaultClient) and the automatic client-credentials mint and refresh grant (through c.HTTPClient, whose CheckRedirect follows a 307 to another host) replayed the token request body, the client secret included, to whatever host a redirect from the token URL named. Printed before press 4.33.5, which routes every token request through cliutil.OAuthTokenHTTPClient (a token client that follows same-origin hops only); this back-ports that file verbatim and uses it at the same call sites. TestAuthLoginRefusesATokenRedirectToAnotherOrigin and TestTokenMintRefusesARedirectToAnotherOrigin failed on the previous commit (the second host received the token request) and pass now. The host compare is also hardened (see the newer-print entries): an IP literal compares exactly, IPv6 zone included; a DNS name folds ASCII case only.
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: Press-side: auth.go.tmpl and client.go.tmpl in press 4.33.5 already route token requests through cliutil.OAuthTokenHTTPClient; oauthTokenSameOrigin should compare IP literals exactly (zone included) and fold ASCII case only for DNS names.

handfixes.summary: export --output closes its output file (written through the credential kit) on every return, including an API error: the open no longer shadows RunE's named err
handfixes.why: The generated `f, err := openExportOutput(...)` inside the --output block declared a new err, so the deferred close tested that inner (nil) err and never ran when the export returned an API error. With the output chokepoint the file is a filter pipe, and the unclosed pipe kept the process from exiting: `export clients --output f.jsonl` after a 401 hung (TestExportOutputReturnsAfterAnAPIError, seen failing 3 of 4 runs). Fleet note: every connector that took the ported chokepoint edit on export.go carries the same shadowing. Ported to nerdio from the gradient 4.34.2 reprint (one credential layer across the fleet). One anchored line in doctor.go (tools/apply_edits.py). Seen failing: seen/r1-p2-doctor-pair-verdict-seen-failing.log. handfixes.summary: A credential goes only to the scheme, host and port configured for it: every API request and the bearer token to the API base URL's origin (the operator's NMM instance); the Entra token URL's origin only receives POST <token path> carrying no bearer token; every redirect hop stays on the origin of the request it follows; a non-ASCII or unparseable host never matches; `auth login`'s own token client is pinned the same way
handfixes.why: Work-order credential rule (host pinning). The NMM API (per-MSP instance) and its token endpoint (Microsoft Entra ID, the operator's tenant) are different hosts, so the guard has two pins (the pax8/appdirect shape). Applied through registerClientHook (every CLI, novel and MCP client) and one anchored line in root.go oauthHTTPClient (tools/apply_credential_rules.py).

handfixes.summary: The shipped base_url host (nmm.example.com) pins nothing: every API request is refused before it is sent, and the error names NERDIO_BASE_URL, so a bearer token is never sent to a placeholder name
handfixes.why: Every MSP runs its own NMM instance; there is no vendor-global API. The press ships https://nmm.example.com as base_url, and before this a forgotten NERDIO_BASE_URL sent the bearer token to whoever answers for that name (doctor already refused it; ordinary commands did not).

handfixes.summary: Every token request (automatic mint, refresh grant, auth login) resolves its URL through client.ResolveNerdioTokenURL: the operator's NERDIO_TOKEN_URL (or token_url in a trusted config) only; unset, still the YOUR_TENANT_ID placeholder, userinfo-bearing or not http(s) means nothing is posted (ErrNoNerdioTokenURL names the variable)
handfixes.why: Press 4.34.2 (and 4.24) hard-coded https://login.microsoftonline.com/YOUR_TENANT_ID/oauth2/v2.0/token as the fallback at all three token sites, so an operator who forgot NERDIO_TOKEN_URL posted the client secret to a URL naming no tenant of theirs. tools/apply_edits.py re-points the three sites.

handfixes.summary: The token request's scope is exactly NERDIO_OAUTH_SCOPE (the NMM application's bare '<app-id>/.default'); unset means nothing is posted and ErrNoNerdioScope names the variable; the scope is never derived from the caller's own client ID
handfixes.why: Press 4.34.2 (and 4.24) defaulted the scope to api://<client_id>/.default: the caller's own application, not the NMM API, with the api:// prefix that triggers AADSTS500011 (the documented trap). Both scope resolvers (client.go, auth.go) read client.ResolveNerdioScope (tools/apply_edits.py); the automatic mint and auth login refuse before sending.

handfixes.summary: A read whose purpose is to return a customer secret the operator asked for by name (devices laps: LAPS password; devices bitlocker-keys; the secure-variables lists) prints it to the caller and writes it nowhere: its path is no sync partition, so the data-source chokepoint never caches or stores it; the response cache is off; secure-variables is not synced (spec syncable: false)
handfixes.why: Sync stored secure-variable values in SQLite at 4.24 and 4.34.2 (default sync set), and every generated `devices` read wrote through into the devices partition, LAPS passwords included. Holding these fields as connector credentials would withhold the very answer each command exists to give, so the guard does not hold them (nerdioTenantSecretPath) and the store never sees them (store-partition-follows-path).

handfixes.summary: A field, flag or header name whose only credential word is 'session' (sessionId, sessionState, sessionHostName, sessionTimeouts) is Azure Virtual Desktop data, not a credential; sessionToken, sessionSecret, sessionCookie and sessionKey stay credentials. handfixes.summary: The shared credential kit (tools/maintainer/credkit, vendored at cli/internal/credkit) is wired by hand and replaces this connector's own credential layer. internal/credwire/declarations.go holds the one Declarations literal; each main starts with credkit.Start and ends with credkit.Exit, and every exit of the MCP main returns through it; the API client (client.OutboundGuard, under the origin pin), feedback, deliver and probe clients go through credkit.Transport; every file write outside the 0600 credential store and config goes through the kit; the MCP stdio and HTTP servers pass credkit.MCPIn, MCPOut, MCPHTTP and MCPTools; the MCP mirror runs the CLI with credkit.RunCommand; isTerminal asks credkit.Terminal. The client pair and refresh token may go to base_url and Entra ID's sign-in hosts only; the minted token is held where it is minted (minted:access_token) and the pair where a mint starts (minted:client-pair). The kit's base_url is the one the run really uses (config.SelectedBaseURL for the last --config under the last --home, then NERDIO_BASE_URL), set for Start only and restored by credwire.AfterStart.
handfixes.why: One contract, one matcher and one set of sinks replace the connector-only copies, and a matcher fix reaches this connector by vendoring. Tests: internal/credwire/leak_test.go on the built binaries, each seen failing on the pre-kit build (.review/seen-*.log): a malformed config's credential in startup output, the client pair to a token URL on a third origin, a piece of the minted token echoed by a response, --stdin bodies and run profiles. The nerdioblackbox suite runs every output, file and network sink against an echoing fake and a quiet control. Retires secret-echo-decoded-funnel, output-chokepoint, file-sinks-withheld, store-never-keeps-secrets, mcp-protocol-messages-withheld, network-sinks-withheld, startup-output-held-first, mcp-held-arguments-refused, undecoded-encodings-every-alignment, held-forms-in-every-encoding, every-text-encoding-withheld, outbound-split-parts-refused, auth-carrier-names-and-shapes-held, derived-credential-parts-held, output-units-reassembled, journal-entry-withheld-as-written, base85-family-withheld, short-held-values-matched-anywhere, output-split-across-deliveries, holder-holds-every-credential-part, decoded-forms-withheld, markup-credential-subtree-held, response-credentials-held: replaced by the shared credential kit (entries removed: the ledger's retired list only takes retirements tools/maintainer/fleet_handfixes.json backs). Behavior change: a unit that carries a held value is withheld whole with the kit's notice, where the old layer redacted the value in place; a token URL on an origin other than base_url and Entra ID's hosts is refused. claimLegacyUnscopedDB reads its owner marker through filepath.Clean (the form blackpoint carries), because editing that function moved it off its reviewed G304 suppression.

handfixes.summary: The MCP server parses its flags with ContinueOnError on a copy of the arguments: -h prints the usage and exits 0, a bad flag prints its error and exits 2, and every exit (an HTTP start without NERDIO_MCP_HTTP_TOKEN, a refused bind, a --config or --home it does not take) returns through credkit.Exit, which delivers stderr first.
handfixes.why: stderr is a pipe the kit drains on a goroutine; flag.Parse's own os.Exit left before the pipe delivered, so -h printed no usage and a refused start exited with no reason. TestMCPExitDeliversItsMessage builds the real binary (.exe on Windows) and was seen failing on the pre-kit build (.review/seen-mcp-exit-fail.log).
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: Press-side: generate the MCP main with ContinueOnError flag parsing and one exit path.

handfixes.summary: The declared response fields (access_token, refresh_token, id_token, accessToken, refreshToken, idToken, sessionToken) are held by the kit as a response passes its transport, and the client replaces each by name with "[withheld]" at its one success return and in an error body, so the rest of the answer (an AVD session, an account) stays usable. A tenant secret (LAPS password, BitLocker key, secure-variable value) is under none of these names and is shown to the caller who asked.
handfixes.why: A declared field's value is held, so without the replacement every sink would withhold the whole answer. TestDeclarationsMatchTheMaskedFields keeps the two lists one.

handfixes.why: A hand-written body parser was a second reader of what the kit already holds. The cost: a preview of a --stdin body, and a vendor answer repeating part of it, are withheld, and the write still happens.
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: Press-side: generate StdinFlags and the compaction with the kit wiring.

A profile's name and its other values stay data.

handfixes.summary: sync wraps the event writer its parallel workers share in syncSerialWriter (internal/cli/sync_event_writer.go), so two workers never call Write on it at once.
handfixes.why: The generated sync hands cmd.OutOrStdout() (or ErrOrStderr() in machine output) to every --concurrency worker, and each writes sync_start, progress and error events. os.Stdout tolerates that; the writers --deliver (a mirror into a bytes.Buffer) and --receipt-file / --audit-dir (a running SHA-256) install do not, nor does an in-process caller's buffer: Windows CI on PR #655 panicked in bytes.Buffer.grow from syncResource, and go test -race found 28 races on veeam. TestSyncWorkerPoolSerializesEventWrites pins it. A reprint regenerates sync.go and drops the wrap; tools/maintainer/replay_handfixes.py re-applies it (fleet_handfixes.json sync-event-writer-serialized).
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: Press-side (mvanhorn/cli-printing-press#5369): the sync template should serialize the event writer its top-level worker pool shares, as its dependent path already does with lockedWriter.
